cases.purpose: Physically inspect the specified SSD installation, verify the device is seated correctly, perform the approved removal/reinstallation check, and confirm the expected storage device remains detectable without new errors after the action.
preconditions: A qualified operator has physical access to the DUT and the approved SSD service, slot, and power-isolation or hot-swap procedure.
The SSD identity, slot or bay mapping, and the expected post-cycle detection criterion are provided.
Backup/data-protection requirements, ESD controls, and the operator checklist/photo locations are defined.
pre_check_commands: Before any physical action, preserve the current approved storage enumeration, host availability, and kernel/BMC/SEL evidence with a timestamp; do not clear logs or alter mounts/data.
safety_checks: Do not remove or insert the SSD while energized unless the platform explicitly supports and approves that hot-swap operation.
Do not force the drive, disturb unrelated storage, mount or write data, or continue after bent contacts, damage, abnormal heat, or unexpected device loss.
Do not clear dmesg, syslog, or SEL; preserve evidence of any storage or link event.
cases.test_command: A qualified operator identifies the SSD and slot, inspects seating and connector condition, performs the approved power-isolated or hot-swap removal/reinstallation check, and records ease of handling and photos. After operator confirmation, the agent may collect the approved storage enumeration and kernel/BMC error evidence without mounting or modifying data.
risk_notes: The primary checks are physical seating and removal/reinstallation, which cannot be verified remotely.
Improper SSD handling can damage the drive, connector, backplane, or chassis and can interrupt storage availability or data access.
The source does not identify the SSD, slot, protocol, or safe hot-swap mode; those parameters must not be guessed.
Clearing logs would erase evidence of a storage link or device failure, so a preserved baseline is required.
expected_evidence: Operator checklist and timestamped photos of the identified SSD, slot, seating, and connector condition.
Operator record that removal/reinstallation was completed under the approved procedure without force.
Pre/post approved storage enumeration, expected device identity, host availability, and kernel/BMC/SEL delta without data writes.
post_check_commands: After operator confirmation, collect the approved non-destructive storage/device enumeration and verify the expected SSD identity remains available.
Collect kernel and BMC/SEL entries after the baseline timestamp; do not mount, format, benchmark, or write the device.
logs_to_collect: Host availability and device identity evidence
Kernel and BMC/SEL delta with prior logs preserved
blocked_conditions: No qualified operator, physical access, SSD identity, slot map, or approved removal/reinstallation procedure.
Hot-swap is unsupported or the power-isolation procedure is unavailable.
Missing backup/data-protection confirmation, damaged connector/drive, forced fit, unexpected device loss, or new unexplained storage errors.
The expected post-cycle storage identity or pass criterion is not defined.

cases.purpose: Inspect the specified node, component, and cable connections to verify correct physical positioning and connection, with no mismatch, bent pin, or cable-routing defect.
preconditions: A qualified operator has physical DUT access and the approved connection drawing, node/component list, and cable-routing criteria.
Every connection target and expected orientation or mating part is identified.
Power isolation, ESD controls, and the required connection checklist/photo locations are available.
pre_check_commands: Before physical handling, record the current device and BMC state and preserve relevant kernel/BMC/SEL evidence when post-action comparison is required; do not clear logs.
safety_checks: Do not unplug, reseat, or mate a connection while energized unless the platform explicitly permits that operation.
Do not force a connector or continue after mismatch, bent pin, damaged latch, pinched cable, or unsafe routing near heat or moving parts.
Do not clear dmesg, syslog, or SEL; preserve the baseline before inspection or any approved physical action.
cases.test_command: A qualified operator checks every listed node, component, and cable against the approved drawing, verifies mating, orientation, pin condition, routing, and strain relief, and records photos. If a plug cycle is part of the approved procedure, the operator performs it and reports the physical result; the agent may collect only permitted post-action evidence.
risk_notes: The source criteria are visual and mechanical properties of many physical connections, so SSH cannot prove them.
Wrong mating, bent pins, damaged latches, or poor routing can damage connected hardware or cause intermittent or complete loss of service.
The source lacks a complete connection list and asks to clear logs; identity/criteria must be supplied and existing evidence preserved.
expected_evidence: Connection checklist covering each node, component, and cable target.
Timestamped photos showing mating, orientation, pin/latch condition, and routing.
Operator record of any approved plug-cycle result plus preserved pre/post kernel/BMC/SEL or device evidence.
post_check_commands: After operator confirmation, collect approved device/BMC enumeration and the kernel/BMC/SEL delta from the baseline timestamp.
Verify the management path and expected devices remain available when the connection procedure defines those post-conditions.
logs_to_collect: Kernel and BMC/SEL delta with historical records preserved
blocked_conditions: No qualified operator, physical access, approved connection drawing, or complete target list.
Connection identity/orientation, safe handling procedure, or acceptance criteria are ambiguous.
Mismatch, bent pin, damaged latch, forced fit, pinched/unsafe cable routing, unexpected device loss, or new hardware error.
Loss of management access after an approved physical action.

cases.blast_radius: Multiple node/component/cable connections, attached hardware, chassis availability, cooling/airflow around routes, and BMC/host access.
cases.recovery_procedure: Stop on mismatch, bent pin, damaged latch, forced fit, unsafe routing, missing device, new hardware error, or lost management access. Preserve photos and logs, do not force or repeat the connection action, and escalate to the hardware owner.
manual_steps: Operator maps each listed connection to the approved drawing and inspects it.
Operator records physical condition and performs only the approved plug cycle, if applicable.
cases.openhands_instruction: Do not attempt or claim the physical connection inspection. Validate the target list, drawing, and safety procedure, wait for operator evidence, then collect only approved post-action device/BMC and log evidence. End user decides PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.

cases.purpose: Inspect the liquid-cooling connector for correct seating and perform the approved connection cycle while preserving physical evidence of the connector and cooling loop condition.
preconditions: A qualified operator has physical access to the DUT and the approved liquid-cooling connector service and isolation procedure.
The connector location, mating counterpart, coolant-loop handling requirements, and physical acceptance criteria are identified.
Cooling-system shutdown/drain or isolation, ESD controls, spill containment, and photo/checklist requirements are available.
pre_check_commands: Before physical handling, preserve current BMC thermal/cooling telemetry, host availability, and relevant kernel/BMC/SEL evidence with a timestamp; do not clear logs.
safety_checks: Do not disconnect or reconnect a liquid-cooling connector while the loop is pressurized or the platform procedure otherwise prohibits it.
Stop immediately for coolant residue, wetness, damaged seal or latch, abnormal pressure/temperature, forced mating, spill, or loss of management access.
Keep coolant away from energized electronics, use the approved containment and cleanup procedure, and do not clear logs or erase evidence.
cases.test_command: A qualified operator inspects the specified liquid-cooling connector and seal area, performs the approved isolated disconnect/reconnect or seating check, and records connector condition and photos. After operator confirmation, the agent may collect approved thermal/cooling telemetry and post-action system evidence.
risk_notes: The source criterion is physical connector seating and the DeepSeek review identifies the cooling-loop seal as the target; a remote agent cannot inspect or verify it.
A disturbed liquid connector can leak coolant onto electronics, interrupt cooling, or cause thermal and electrical damage.
The source does not define a leak/pressure threshold, so the agent must not invent a remote pass condition; physical inspection and the platform procedure govern.
Clearing logs would remove evidence of thermal or cooling events, so the baseline must be preserved.
expected_evidence: Operator checklist and timestamped photos of connector seating, latch/seal condition, and any coolant residue.
Operator record that the approved connection action was completed without force or leak.
Pre/post BMC thermal/cooling telemetry and kernel/BMC/SEL delta, when the platform exposes those signals.
post_check_commands: After operator confirmation, collect approved BMC thermal, fan, pump, coolant, and leak-sensor status where available.
Verify host/BMC reachability and collect the post-action kernel/BMC/SEL delta without deleting prior records.
logs_to_collect: Kernel and BMC/SEL delta with preserved history
blocked_conditions: No qualified operator, physical access, connector identity, cooling isolation procedure, spill containment, or acceptance criteria.
Pressurized or energized handling is not explicitly approved, or the approved drain/isolation method is unavailable.
Coolant leak/residue, damaged seal/latch, spill, abnormal thermal/cooling telemetry, unexpected shutdown, or lost management access.
The platform has no defined safe recovery path for a disturbed cooling connector.

deepseek_original_review.ai_commands: -- Connector: liquid-cooling connector inspection verifies the physical connector seating/seal; human visual/physical check at the cooling loop.
deepseek_original_review.ai_logs_output: operator visually inspects + records the cooling connector; agent cannot inspect hardware.

cases.gpt_second_review_findings: DeepSeek's NO classification is correct and specifically identifies this row as a liquid-cooling connector seating/seal inspection, not a generic software connector check. GPT adds the cooling-loop hazards: require pressure/isolation and spill controls, preserve thermal evidence, and stop on wetness or seal damage. Automation is limited to approved post-action telemetry collection after the operator completes the physical inspection; the source does not provide a measurable leak or pressure criterion to infer remotely.
cases.blast_radius: Liquid-cooling connector and seal, coolant loop, nearby electronics, thermal control, DUT availability, and BMC/host access.
cases.recovery_procedure: Stop on any leak, wetness, damaged seal, spill, abnormal thermal state, or lost management access. Isolate power/cooling only under the approved platform procedure, preserve photos and logs, do not reconnect or repeat the action, and escalate to the cooling/hardware owner.
manual_steps: Operator identifies the liquid-cooling connector and verifies the approved isolation/containment procedure.
Operator inspects and performs the approved connection check, recording seal condition, evidence, and photos.
cases.openhands_instruction: Do not attempt or claim the physical cooling-connector action. Validate the isolation and spill procedure, wait for operator confirmation and photos, then collect only approved cooling telemetry and post-action logs. End user decides PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
